metadata.name: Texas Aviation Capital Improvement Program (ACIP)
metadata.agency: Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) Aviation Division; Texas Transportation Commission
metadata.source_citation: TxDOT Aviation Capital Improvement Program 2026-2028. Source PDF: https://www.txdot.gov/content/dam/docs/division/avn/acip-2026-2028-exec-summary.pdf. Objectives in priority order (per Texas Transportation Commission): (1) Enhance safety, (2) Preserve existing facilities, (3) Respond to present needs, (4) Provide for anticipated needs.

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 8 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded Texas as multiplicative model with the 5 documented project categories at the top, plus airport activity and federal leverage as secondary criteria.
decisions_log.rationale: TxDOT explicitly lists 5 project categories in priority order (Safety > Preservation > Capacity > New Access > New Capacity). Multiplicative captures the strong ordering. Texas Transportation Commission objectives map directly to these categories.

criteria.label: Project Category (Commission Priority Order)
criteria.description: Texas Transportation Commission-set priority categories. Only one selected.

subcategories.label: Safety - Make facility safe for aircraft operations
Capacity - Accommodate more aircraft / higher activity
New Access - Air access to previously unserved area
New Capacity - New airport to relieve area congestion

criteria.label: Federal Funding Leverage
criteria.description: Texas leverages FAA AIP funding heavily. Projects with federal funding committed get priority.

criteria.label: Project Urgency
criteria.description: Risk if project not done in current programming cycle.

governance.approval_process: TxDOT Aviation prepares 3-year ACIP. Texas Transportation Commission approves annually. ACIP updated continually. Combines federal AIP and state projects.

disclaimer: Encoded from TxDOT ACIP 2026-2028 Executive Summary. The 5 project categories and their priority order are documented; specific numerical scoring is internal to the Aviation Division. Point values are inferred to preserve the documented priority ordering. Texas stakeholders should calibrate to TxDOT internal scoring before adoption.
